throughSec.description: End of the actually ingested prefix; not the eventual match end.

DirectorFactTrace.description: The serializable baseline; no camera or audio sidecar is required.

streamId.description: Caller-owned match/connection epoch. Start a new journal on reset.

sequence.description: Monotonically increasing across all kinds, starting at 1.

id.description: Stable within this stream; identity survives later enrichment.

revision.description: Starts at 1; each later record replaces this fact's entire value.

timeSec.description: When the underlying event happened, in game/demo seconds.

availableAtSec.description: When this revision became available, in the same clock domain.

value.description: Raw director evidence, not a commentary cue. Missing attribution is unknown. Existing inference fields keep their DirectorDataset meaning: e.g. dropKind=pass can be inferred from proximity, and airborne alone does not prove a mid-air skill shot. No camera visibility is implied.

DirectorFactRecord.description: One immutable revision of a fact, in the order it became available.

teamAffinity.description: For flag events: whether the recorder's team or enemy team was involved.

killer.description: For kill/death events: name of the killer.

victim.description: For kill/death events: name of the victim.

weapon.description: For kill/death events: weapon or damage type (e.g. "disc", "ground").

capturer.description: For flag-cap events: name of the player who captured.

actor.description: For flag-grab/flag-drop/flag-return events: the player responsible (unset for auto-returns and recorder-perspective events).

flagTeamName.description: For flag events: name of the flag's team.

previousName.description: For rename events: the name before the change (`actor` is the name after).

raw.description: The same names as sent, color codes included — the official clan tag is the color-7 segment. For display only; matching uses the stripped fields above.

secondsUntil.description: match-countdown only: seconds until the announced kickoff.

pos.description: Torque-space position correlated from entity samples, when known.

dropKind.description: Flag drops only — the carrier's intent, from chat-message order and teammate proximity/pickup: "died" (killed holding it), "thrown" (deliberate), or "pass" (thrown to teammates).

TeamAffinity.description: Relationship of the event to the recorder's team.

killerTargetId.description: Nearest opposing player at the moment of death, if any: the likely killer, and the other half of a highlight shot.

weapon.description: Damage type from the kill message ("disc", "laser", "shocklance", …), or inferred from ordnance in flight nearby as the fallback.

airborne.description: Nothing under the victim's feet when they died — a mid-air kill, the game's signature skill shot when paired with a disc/mortar.

speed.description: Victim's speed at death (u/s), from their last two samples.

midair.description: A verified MID-AIR: the server's own skill-shot announcement ("X hit a mid air shot.") correlated to this death's killer. Vehicle rams, splash and snipes never set this.

headshot.description: A sniper-rifle headshot, from the server's announcement.

DirectorDeath.description: A player death seen in the entity stream (damageState alive → not), which — unlike chat kill messages — is available for EVERY player in both observer and first-person recordings.

targetId.description: The shooter's target id, when the name resolved.

SkillShot.description: A server-announced skill shot (chat kind "server", color code 5): "X hit a mid air shot. [69m, Spinfusor]" or "X hit a sniper rifle headshot." Authoritative — no inference. `lethal` marks the ones correlated to a death (whose kill event then carries the flag).

teamId.description: Owning team, from the ghost's own sensor group (StreamEntity .teamId) — the game's answer, not an inference from position.

name.description: Commentary name ("spider clamp turret", "generator", …) — never a raw shape filename; placement variants (wall/floor/ceiling, indoor/outdoor) are deliberately erased.

StructureTransition.description: A base structure's damageState change (0 = Enabled, 1 = Disabled, 2 = Destroyed) — the only observer-visible signal for generator and turret kills, which have no broadcast chat message.
